definition: Flagrant means offensive, egregious; glaringly bad.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word flagrant. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know flagrant should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The judges ruled the bakery sticker still on the 'homemade' pie a flagrant breach of the bake-off's one rule.
Overt is far milder than flagrant — it just means done in the open, with no judgment attached.
Blatant stops a step short of flagrant: both are impossible to miss, but flagrant adds the offense — a blatant hint is loud, a flagrant foul is loud and wrong.

Glaring means impossible to overlook — a glaring error announces itself from across the room. It measures visibility alone. Flagrant measures visibility and guilt at once: a flagrant violation is both unmissable and inexcusable, while a glaring one may be an innocent mistake.

Egregious means conspicuously, shockingly bad — an egregious blunder, an egregious abuse of trust. It grades the badness alone. Flagrant grades badness and openness together: a flagrant offense happens in plain view, while an egregious one may shock only once it is uncovered.
